authors.author: edwards
authors.name: Jonathan Edwards (1703–1758)
authors.title: The Works of President Edwards, with a Memoir of His Life
authors.editorialHistory: Posthumous Dwight collection, incorporating earlier editorial work by John Erskine, Edward Williams and Jonathan Edwards the younger. The younger Edwards is a manuscript editor here, not the preacher. Editorial consolidation is identified at component level.
authors.catalogPublisher: New York: G. & C. & H. Carvill
authors.boundary: Sermon-bearing volumes 1, 3, 5–8 and 10 of the ten-volume Dwight collection; volume 9 retained as a screened non-sermon contextual volume. Not a complete surviving-manuscript census.

authors.name: George Whitefield
authors.title: The Works of the Reverend George Whitefield
authors.editorialHistory: Posthumous collected edition. Both sermon-volume title pages read 1772; their contents mark certain sermons as first publication from the author's manuscripts. Specific editor identity not independently established from these two volumes.

authors.boundary: Both sermon volumes of the six-volume collected works; retain manuscript-first-publication markers. Later Gurney shorthand collections are separate witnesses, not automatic duplicates.

authors.author: newton
authors.name: John Newton
authors.title: The Works of the Rev. John Newton
authors.editorialHistory: Posthumous New York reprint from the London edition directed by Newton's executors. Volume VI's advertisement distinguishes author-approved letters, periodical essays, and the previously printed 1800 sermon. Messiah is author-abridged; the 1800 sermon was reconstructed from memory, as its advertisement states.
authors.catalogPublisher: New York: Williams & Whiting; Samuel Whiting
authors.boundary: Volumes 2–6 screened for sermon material; preserve Messiah as a complete 50-discourse series and distinguish Discourses Intended for the Pulpit from documented delivery.

authors.author: ryle
authors.name: J. C. Ryle (1816–1900)
authors.title: The Christian Race and Other Sermons; The Two Bears and Other Sermons for Children
authors.editorialHistory: Christian Race: selected from Ryle's manuscripts by T. J. Madden with Ryle's authorization, as Madden's March 1, 1900 preface states. Selection was not by Ryle personally. Publication day relative to Ryle's death is unestablished. Two Bears: 1869 lifetime printing, including pastoral pieces alongside sermon-form addresses.
authors.catalogPublisher: London: Hodder & Stoughton (Christian Race); London and Ipswich: William Hunt (Two Bears), verified on title pages
authors.boundary: Two separately published sermon collections; exclude Herbert Edward Ryle, and distinguish collection publication from individual delivery.
